3.text: their forefathers had no clay kettles, and the meat was roasted on large flat

4.text: stones heated for the purpose. The Lamut tell the same story of their ances-

5.text: tors; but such a method of cooking is possible only within the borders of the

6.text: forest, where the supply of fuel is abundant. On the tundra and on the

7.text: treeless coast a method of cooking that requires less fuel must always have

8.text: been in use. Therefore it seems probable that the lamp and the kettle were

9.text: in use in former times as well as now.

10.text: The Yukaghir and the Kamchadal used to boil their meat and fish in

11.text: bark or wooden vessels by means of heated stones. This method of boiling

12.text: meat is still used occasionally by the hunter, who carries no kettle, and who

13.text: may boil his meat in the old way. The Kamchadal of Central Kamchatka

14.text: extract the fish-oil of Salmo sanguinolentus by trying out the fish in a dug-out

16.text: At present the Chukchee use little roasted meat. They hardly know how

17.text: to roast it properly. Fish and lungs, which are sometimes roasted near the

18.text: fire, are always covered with ashes, charred from without, and quite raw

19.text: within. The Yukaghir and Kamchadal roast fish and meat very well on thin

20.text: wooden spits stuck into the ground near the fire.

21.text: RAW AND PUTRID MEAT AND CARRION. — Raw, frozen meat is eaten by

22.text: the Reindeer Chukchee and all the neighboring tribes. The Arctic people

23.text: consider meat that is raw and hard-frozen just as palatable as cooked meat.

24.text: I must acknowledge that I soon learned to eat it and to like its taste.

25.text: Especially when we had to live for a long time exclusively on fat fish, with

26.text: not so much as a pinch of salt to season it, we found this diet more tolerable

27.text: when the fish was eaten raw and frozen hard.

28.text: Liver and kidneys, heart, tendons of the legs, gristle of the nose, eyes,

29.text: and marrow are consumed raw summer and winter, immediately after the

30.text: reindeer has been slaughtered. Blood is also consumed raw, fresh, or half-

31.text: putrid. The Chukchee are averse to eating other parts of the animal raw;

32.text: and I know of cases where a herdsman who had no kettle killed one buck

33.text: after another, and ate only those parts that are considered fit to be eaten raw,

34.text: leaving all the rest of the meat to spoil.

35.text: The Reindeer Chukchee, and especially the herdsmen, however, are not

36.text: very particular as to their food. They eat the maggots of the reindeer-fly,

37.text: and various herbs which taste to us unsavory or repugnant. In exceptional

38.text: cases they gather toadstools and the green, half-liquid dung of the reindeer

39.text: that has taken to eating leaves in the spring. This is mixed with herbs and

40.text: a little blood or putrid liver, and eaten raw.
